chains.title: Alt T creates a C/EBP site bound by CEBPA in the liver enhancer, raising SORT1 and lowering LDL
chains.element: ENCODE cCRE EH38E1374646 (dELS, chr1:109274794-109275142), overlapping the CELSR2 3'UTR / ENSR1_CDSQQ enhancer

links.claim: The alt T allele is proposed to create a C/EBP-family recognition sequence bound more strongly than ref G. No QBiC-SELEX row, motif scan or liver ChIP peak was returned for this site, so this link remains unsupported by the evidence in hand: E09 explicitly finds no CEBPB peak at the variant in HepG2 (though absence may reflect a missing experiment), while CEBPB peaks in A549, HeLa-S3, IMR-90 and MCF-7 show only that the sequence is C/EBP-accessible in some cells. Within the C/EBP specificity group I name CEBPA rather than CEBPB because the liver effect is hepatocyte-restricted (E08) and CEBPA is the C/EBP member associated with the hepatocyte programme; this choice rests on background knowledge, not on cited expression or ChIP data. CEBPA coverage was never looked up, hence not_checked.
The variant lies inside a distal enhancer-like cCRE (EH38E1374646) with high DNase/H3K27ac z-scores; these are maxima across biosamples, so activity in liver or Hep3B is not shown by this evidence.

In liver the alt T allele is associated with higher SORT1 expression (NES +1.27, p 3.1e-54), the largest liver eQTL effect of the variant, and SORT1 is the top L2G gene (0.99) for the lipid GWAS; the eQTL is association, not a demonstrated enhancer-promoter link.
The effect is seen in liver tissue eQTLs and the expression context is a hepatoma line; literature attributes liver-specific modulation of SORT1 to this variant.

The minor (T) allele sequence enhances SORT1 expression in hepatocytes, and G is the risk allele for high cholesterol/LDL in GWAS, consistent with higher hepatic SORT1 lowering LDL-C and MI risk; the SORT1-to-LDL direction itself is taken from literature statements, not measured here.

chains.title: Same created C/EBP site, but CEBPB is the operative family member
chains.element: cCRE EH38E1374646 (dELS) in the CELSR2 3'UTR region

links.claim: The alt T allele is proposed to create a C/EBP-class motif occupied by CEBPB. The only direct data are Factorbook peaks: CEBPB peaks containing the variant exist in A549, HeLa-S3, IMR-90 and MCF-7, showing the sequence can be CEBPB-bound, but no CEBPB peak was found in HepG2 (possibly because no such experiment exists in that biosample). CEBPB is chosen over CEBPA only because it is the one C/EBP member with observed occupancy at this exact position; coverage not looked up.
The variant lies in the same enhancer-like cCRE with strong (cross-biosample maximum) DNase and H3K27ac signal.
Liver eQTL links the alt allele to higher SORT1 (NES +1.27), the top L2G gene at the locus.
Liver/hepatocyte context from the liver eQTL and the hepatoma expression context; CEBPB abundance in Hep3B was not measured.
Higher hepatic SORT1 from the T allele lowers LDL-C, with G the GWAS risk allele for high cholesterol.

chains.title: Created C/EBP site acts on the proximal genes CELSR2/PSRC1 rather than SORT1
chains.element: cCRE EH38E1374646, within the CELSR2 3'UTR and 9.1 kb from the PSRC1 TSS

links.claim: Same proposed C/EBP site created by the alt T allele, with CEBPA named as the liver-associated family member; no motif or liver ChIP evidence supports this, and the only C/EBP occupancy data are non-hepatic CEBPB peaks.
The variant is a CELSR2 3'UTR variant, sits 9.1 kb from the PSRC1 TSS, and SCREEN lists CELSR2, PSRC1 and MYBPHL as the nearby genes of this cCRE.
The alt allele also raises PSRC1 (NES +1.24) and CELSR2 (NES +1.04) in liver, with CELSR2 L2G 0.98 and PSRC1 0.66, so the proximal genes are co-regulated and could be the effectors rather than SORT1.
The co-regulation is observed in liver tissue; other QTLs for these genes are in muscle, pancreas and esophagus, so hepatocyte specificity is only partly shown.
Altered CELSR2/PSRC1 levels would change hepatic lipoprotein handling and LDL-C, with G the GWAS risk allele; no cited evidence shows a CELSR2 or PSRC1 effect on lipids.

predictions: Knockdown of CELSR2 or PSRC1, but not SORT1, reproduces the apoB/LDL phenotype in hepatocytes

Editing the base changes CELSR2 or PSRC1 with only secondary change in SORT1
falsified_if: SORT1 knockdown alone reproduces the lipid phenotype and CELSR2/PSRC1 knockdown does not

The variant lies in an enhancer-like cCRE (max-over-biosample marks).
Liver eQTL shows the alt allele raises SORT1, which is equally compatible with loss of a repressor on T.

grades_v0.reason: E01 and E03 are VEP and cCRE annotations with no motif, SELEX or ChIP data. Nothing shows that T creates a C/EBP site or that CEBPA binds. The CEBPA choice rests on memory of hepatocyte expression, and coverage was not checked.

E03 shows the variant in a dELS cCRE with high DNase and H3K27ac z-scores, but these are maxima across biosamples and not specific to Hep3B or liver. E01 gives an enhancer regulatory feature. This is epigenomic context only, with no perturbation.

E05 gives L2G 0.99 for SORT1 and a liver sQTL with PIP 0.72. L2G is genetic prioritisation and the sQTL is splicing, not expression. E06a names different lead variants (rs12740347 and rs646776), and E06c only lists SORT1 as a CAD gene. None of these shows that this enhancer acts on SORT1.
The Hep3B context and the liver sQTL fit hepatocytes. E06c does not show hepatic SORT1 function, and no expression or liver-specific enhancer data are cited.

E04 shows G is the risk allele for LDL and cholesterol, consistent with higher SORT1 from T lowering LDL. E06b is a Mendelian randomization colocalisation for MI and diet and says nothing about SORT1 direction. The direction of the SORT1 effect is assumed.
The claim has no evidence, since E01 and E03 are annotations. CEBPB is chosen as 'equally plausible', which is a TF selected from a group without reason, and its expression was not checked.
E03 supports an active cCRE, but only with max-over-biosample marks that are not liver-specific.
E05 L2G supports SORT1 as a genetic candidate but shows no regulatory link from this enhancer. The sQTL concerns splicing.
E05 and E06c do not show CEBPB abundance in hepatocytes. Hepatocyte relevance is inferred from the lipid trait only.
E04 gives the allele direction, but E06b does not bear on SORT1 direction. The link is indirect.
No binding evidence is cited, and CEBPA is assumed. The claim is identical to H1's unsupported one.
E01 shows a CELSR2 3'UTR variant, E02 puts the variant 9.1 kb from the PSRC1 TSS, and E03 lists CELSR2, PSRC1 and MYBPHL as nearby genes. This establishes the proximity claim for the element.

E05 shows CELSR2 L2G 0.96-0.98, and the CELSR2 sQTL (PIP 0.49), PSRC1 eQTL (PIP 0.41) and tuQTL (PIP 0.32) are modest. The claim of colocalising QTLs is overstated because these are fine-mapping PIPs, and the tissues are non-hepatic for PSRC1 and CELSR2 sQTL. SORT1 has stronger L2G, so the data do not favour CELSR2 or PSRC1.
E05 cites no hepatocyte-specific co-regulation of CELSR2 or PSRC1. Several QTLs are in muscle, pancreas and esophagus.
E04 gives the G risk allele direction. E06a names different lead variants and shows no CELSR2 or PSRC1 effect on lipids.
E01 says nothing about HNF4A or any repressor. The claim is speculative, with no HNF4A motif, ChIP or expression evidence and coverage not checked.
E03 supports an active enhancer-like cCRE, but 'hepatic' is not shown because the marks are maxima across biosamples.
E05 L2G supports SORT1 genetically only, with no regulatory evidence.
The liver sQTL fits hepatocytes, but nothing shows HNF4A activity in this context.
E04 gives the risk-allele direction and E06b is not cited. The direction is consistent with H1 and so cannot discriminate between hypotheses.

grades_final.reason: No QBiC-SELEX, motif, or liver ChIP evidence for CEBPA or any C/EBP gain on T. E09 shows only CEBPB peaks in non-liver cells and no HepG2 peak, so it does not bear on CEBPA. CEBPA is chosen from the C/EBP group on background knowledge, and its coverage was never looked up (suggest a qbic_tf_detail lookup of CEBPA). E07 only retrieves hits for a C/EBP query and gives no direct quote of C/EBP binding.

E03 places the variant in dELS cCRE EH38E1374646, and E01 shows an enhancer regulatory feature. The z-scores are maxima across biosamples, so hepatic activity is not shown, and there is no perturbation of the element.

E08 shows a strong liver eQTL (alt T raises SORT1, NES +1.27), and E05 gives SORT1 L2G 0.99 and a liver sQTL PIP 0.72. This is genetic association with direction consistent with E07b. PSRC1 and CELSR2 have similar effects, so SORT1 is not uniquely resolved, and no enhancer-promoter link or perturbation ties the element to SORT1.

E08 gives liver eQTLs. E07a/E07b report liver and hepatocyte modulation of SORT1 by rs12740374, with the minor allele enhancing expression in hepatocytes. The Hep3B context is not itself tested, but the hepatocyte claim is directly shown.

E04 shows G as the effect allele for high cholesterol and total/LDL cholesterol, which agrees with T raising SORT1 (E07b) and lowering LDL. E07c and E07a give the SORT1 locus-LDL association. The causal SORT1-to-LDL direction is not shown in the provided evidence. There is no MI-specific evidence apart from E06b's MI colocalisation, and the chain depends on an unverified TF mechanism.

E09 shows CEBPB peaks containing the variant in A549, HeLa-S3, IMR-90 and MCF-7, which is direct occupancy at this position for CEBPB. These cells are non-hepatic, there is no HepG2 peak, and nothing shows allelic preference or alt-allele gain. This is better than H1's binding link but is not allelic evidence. CEBPB coverage was not looked up (suggest a qbic_tf_detail lookup).
E03 shows an enhancer-like cCRE with strong cross-biosample maxima. Hepatic activity is not shown and there is no perturbation.
The liver eQTL (E08, SORT1 NES +1.27) and L2G (E05) are association-level evidence. PSRC1 and CELSR2 have comparable effects, and no evidence links CEBPB to the SORT1 effect.

E08 and E07a support hepatocyte or liver relevance of the variant effect. The claim ties it to CEBPB in hepatocytes, but CEBPB expression in Hep3B and in liver is not shown and the only CEBPB occupancy is in non-hepatic cells.
E07b and E04 are directionally consistent: T raises SORT1 and G is the LDL risk allele. The SORT1-to-LDL causality is not measured in the provided evidence and does not depend on CEBPB.

No motif, SELEX, or liver ChIP evidence for CEBPA. E09 shows only non-hepatic CEBPB peaks, which cannot be used as evidence for CEBPA. CEBPA coverage was not looked up (suggest a qbic_tf_detail lookup).

E01 shows a CELSR2 3'UTR variant, E02 gives the 9.1 kb distance to PSRC1, and E03 lists CELSR2, PSRC1 and MYBPHL as nearby genes of the cCRE. This is proximity-based context and does not show element-gene regulation.

E08 shows alt raising PSRC1 (NES +1.24) and CELSR2 (NES +1.04) in liver, and E05 gives L2G for CELSR2 (0.98) and PSRC1 (0.66). This is association-level evidence, and SORT1 is equally or more strongly supported, so CELSR2 as the effector is not distinguished. No perturbation evidence is cited.
E08 shows liver eQTLs for CELSR2 and PSRC1. The other QTLs in E05 are in muscle, pancreas and esophagus, so hepatocyte specificity of the effect is only partly shown.
The claim says no cited evidence shows a CELSR2 or PSRC1 effect on lipids. E04 shows only the variant-LDL association and not the gene mediating it, so it does not support the claim.

No motif, SELEX, ChIP or expression evidence for HNF4A at this site. E09 concerns CEBPB in non-liver cells and does not bear on HNF4A. The HNF4A coverage claim is not shown by any lookup (suggest a qbic_tf_detail lookup).

E03 shows an enhancer-like cCRE with cross-biosample maxima. This is context only and says nothing about repression by HNF4A. An enhancer-like annotation is also not obviously compatible with a repressor model.

E08 shows the alt allele raising SORT1 in liver, which is association-level and consistent with the direction. The evidence is equally compatible with other mechanisms and does not support a repressor, and it also raises PSRC1 and CELSR2.
E08 shows liver eQTLs, but nothing shows HNF4A activity or expression in the relevant cells and no hepatocyte-specific evidence is cited. It is liver tissue context only.

E04 (G is the risk allele) and E07b (minor allele raises SORT1 in hepatocytes) are direction-consistent with higher SORT1 on T and lower LDL. The evidence is not specific to the HNF4A mechanism, and the SORT1-to-LDL causal direction is not shown in the provided data.
